ideas.truth: We trust things that look considered — quality feels earned when we can see it, not just be told about it.
ideas.moment: The instant a well-made object is caught turning under a single light, revealing craftsmanship a flat photo couldn't show.
ideas.key_frame: Product held tight and off-center against a muted, soft-focus backdrop, one warm light just beginning to graze its edge.

ideas.truth: Anticipation before a moment matters more than the moment itself.
ideas.moment: The last few seconds before someone reaches for it and walks out the door.
ideas.key_frame: Product resting at the edge of a dark surface, a long shadow creeping across the frame like a clock hand.

ideas.truth: Stillness reads as confidence — things that don't need to shout feel expensive.
ideas.moment: A private, gallery-hushed pause where the object simply sits under changing light, saying nothing, needing nothing.
ideas.key_frame: Product centered on a plinth-like surface, dust motes drifting through a single shaft of light.

why: It turns the one static reference photo into a literal, filmable camera move (a single push-in with a synced light sweep) that Veo can execute faithfully without inventing new product details or stacking too many simultaneous motions, delivering 'premium, no people' in one clean take.
treatment: We open close on the product, resting in soft, directional light against a muted backdrop — nothing else competes for attention. The camera begins a slow, deliberate push-in, holding a fixed angle rather than circling the object. As it moves closer, the light shifts — a warm highlight travels across the surface, catching an edge, a curve, a reflection, revealing texture and craftsmanship one beat at a time, driven by the same push. Faint dust motes drift through a background light shaft, barely visible, adding stillness and scale. The push naturally decelerates at the midpoint, then eases to a final resting frame, product centered, light settled, calm. Sound is minimal: a low ambient hum, the whisper of air, a faint metal-glass tick as the highlight crosses the edge. No voice. No people.

decisions.D1_idea: The instant a beautifully made object is caught drawing closer under a single directed light, revealing its craftsmanship as if seen for the first time.
decisions.D2_conflict: No dramatic obstacle — the tension is the visual noise of the ordinary day, from which the object quietly separates itself as something worth stopping the scroll for.
decisions.D3_roles: The viewer is the one who must choose between the ordinary and the considered; the product is both hero and answer — no spokesperson or guide is needed.
decisions.D4_opening: Bold, close image: the product already in a tight, corner-weighted hold against a muted frame — an opening close-up, not mid-action.
decisions.D5_brand: Product is on screen for the full 8 seconds via one continuous shot; no logo/name was supplied, so any brand mark is reserved for the settled final frame in post (see finish notes).
decisions.D6_ask_and_end: No explicit CTA — none was requested. The film ends on the product, settled and centered, carried purely by picture (no voice, no text ask).
decisions.D7_product_truth: Only fact available: the product's form, color and material exactly as shown in the customer's attached photo (source: customer photo). No feature, use-case or claim is stated or implied beyond that.
decisions.D8_deviations: No brand name, logo or CTA copy included — none was supplied, and exact_copy is empty, so inventing any would fabricate a claim; left for a later post step if the client provides assets. Delivered as one 8-second scene (not multiple), matching Veo 3.1's one-scene-per-prompt guidance and the customer's single-reel ask. Removed the orbit component from the camera move (kept in v1) to avoid stacking push + orbit + light-sync + settle into one 8s instruction set, which risked an unstable render.

scenes.prompt: Camera performs one continuous, tripod-smooth slow push-in toward the product across the full 8 seconds, following a single fixed-angle path that gradually decelerates and settles into a still, centered final frame.
scenes.first_frame_still_prompt: Use the customer's provided product photo exactly as supplied for the first frame, preserving its original framing, color, texture, and material details precisely as captured. Keep the product's true form and appearance faithfully intact, showing exactly what the source image already depicts, staying fully consistent with that single reference throughout the opening frame.
scenes.S1_feeling: Quiet admiration — calm awe at something well made.
scenes.S2_first_frame: Tight, corner-weighted close-up on the product against a muted backdrop, one light already grazing its edge — the 'worth a second look' idea is present from frame one, not built toward.
scenes.S3_one_action: One continuous push-in camera move with a light sweep tethered to that same push, running the full 8 seconds and decelerating to natural stillness in the final beat — a single motion instruction, not a compound one.
scenes.S4_new_information: The viewer sees the object drawn nearer with light traveling across it — angles, edges and reflections the flat source photo alone couldn't show — which is the reason to move at all.
scenes.S5_impact: The payoff is the settle: light locks onto the product's most flattering edge and the frame goes still — legible on a silent, small phone scroll as 'this is made well.'

finish.copy_placement: If a brand name/logo is later supplied, place it as a small, high-contrast lockup in the lower third over the final still 1–1.5s only, checked against the darkest patch of that frame, using the brand's own typeface for legibility per guidance.
finish.end_card: Hold on the settled, centered product in its final resting light as the true end frame — no separate end card needed unless a logo is added in post.
finish.music: Yes — a minimal, warm ambient bed with a sparse piano or synth pad, no beat, understated-luxury mood, swelling gently to the midpoint highlight and settling by the final frame.
